name: UXD
who_can_redeem: Users outside restricted jurisdictions may burn UXD through supported protocol interfaces to receive a USD-equivalent amount of supported crypto assets, subject to strategy liquidity and protocol conditions.
redemption_region_notes: Minting and redemption are unavailable in restricted jurisdictions and depend on supported interfaces, network availability, strategy liquidity, slippage, fees, and protocol parameters.
redemption_notes: UXD is not a direct fiat issuer claim. The protocol targets one UXD per one U.S. dollar of managed assets across delta-neutral, lending, overcollateralized, and other approved strategies.
summary: Solana-native U.S.-dollar stablecoin launched in January 2022 with delta-neutral backing and later expanded into a multi-strategy Asset Liability Management model while remaining an active protocol identity.
notes: Growth C / Batch S. Current strategy allocation, EVM production status, governance boundaries, supply, liquidity, and exact ALM implementation milestones remain explicit open items.

name: Dollar on Chain
who_can_redeem: Money on Chain users may redeem DOC through the Rootstock protocol for the U.S.-dollar-equivalent amount of rBTC when protocol state and coverage rules permit.
redemption_region_notes: Access depends on Rootstock, supported wallets and interfaces, protocol coverage state, governance controls, network fees, bridge conditions, and applicable restrictions.
redemption_notes: DOC is a smart-contract-issued protocol asset backed by rBTC rather than a direct fiat issuer claim. The primary mint and redemption system is on Rootstock; the Arbitrum token is a bridged representation.
summary: Bitcoin-collateralized U.S.-dollar stablecoin issued by Money on Chain smart contracts on Rootstock, later bridged to Arbitrum, and active after a temporary April 2026 oracle-related minting and redemption pause was fixed through governance.
notes: Growth C / Batch S. Complete contract-upgrade lineage, current coverage metrics, bridge implementation history, oracle-incident transaction inventory, and emergency-control boundaries remain explicit open items.
